data.name: Hasinika
data.gender_notes: Hasinika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Hasini, a beautiful and charming goddess, is the root of the name Hasinika. This name is derived from the Sanskrit language and holds immense significance in Hindu mythology. The name Hasinika carries the meaning “Goddess Hasi” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Hasinika usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess hasi and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Blessed by the Goddess of Joy
data.etymology: Hasinika belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess Hasi.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hasinika total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hasinika is a beautiful and unique name originating from Hindu mythology. It carries a rich cultural heritage and is associated with the goddess Hasini. This name is not only aesthetically pleasing but also holds great importance in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Hasinika is a name that evokes the essence of the divine goddess Hasini. This name is believed to bestow beauty, grace, and charm upon the bearer. The spiritual significance of this name reflects the Hindu belief in the power and blessings of the gods and goddesses. Hasinika is a reminder that we are all connected to the divine and can draw strength, power, and blessings from the gods and goddesses. This name also reflects the Hindu values of beauty, grace, and the pursuit of inner and outer harmony.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Hasinika: Radiating inner joy and grace. Symbolizes the victorious spirit that conquers sorrows and illuminates the path towards peace and happiness.

historical_references.reference: Hasinika was a queen of the Satavahana dynasty, ruling in the 2nd century AD. She is best known for her patronage of the Buddhist vihara, Amaravati Stupa, which was built during her reign.

Another reference to Hasinika is found in the Jataka tales, a collection of Buddhist stories. In one tale, a king named Hasinika, who ruled over Magadha, shows great generosity and compassion towards a monkey and a snake, which leads to his own enlightenment.

The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
